lines: Caveman browse cuts a web page to 121 tokens instead of 15,704.
Agents talk too much and read huge files.
Caveman is a proxy for coding agents that cuts 65% of tokens by talking like a caveman.
The proxy drops articles but keeps numbers, units, negatives, and code exact.
Run the CSV file through caveman to get 314 tokens saved. The result is 98.9% smaller.
Test output shrinks to 203 tokens exactly. That is a reduction from 18,806.
Adobe Research cut costs by 1.4 to 2.4 times per model using this method.
It shrinks memory files like CLAUDE.md to 46 percent smaller while keeping every heading, code block, and path intact.
It works on Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. Install it with npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman -g.
Apache-2.0 license, 110,358 stars, Adobe Research tested it.
Open your terminal and run this command to add the skill globally.
Save this for when you want fewer tokens.
Caveman says less and works better.
